fanoutqa_033256.x:
Empire State Building :: Architecture :: chunk_0005
The Empire State Building was designed by [Shreve, Lamb and Harmon](/wiki/Shreve,_Lamb_and_Harmon "Shreve, Lamb and Harmon") in the [Art Deco](/wiki/Art_Deco_architecture_of_New_York_City "Art Deco architecture of New York City") style.[[30]](#cite_note-AIA-33) The Empire State Building is 1,250 ft (381 m) tall to its 102nd floor, or 1,453 feet 8+9⁄16 inches (443.092 m) including its 203-foot (61.9 m) pinnacle.[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillisFriedman199814-34) It was the first building in the world to be more than 100 stories tall,[[32]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillisFriedman199856-35) though only the lowest 86 stories are usable. The first through 85th floors contain 2.158 million square feet (200,500 m2) of commercial and office space, while the 86th floor contains an observatory.[[33]](#cite_note-Reynolds_p._290-36)[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillisFriedman199814-34)[[34]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELandmarks_Preservation_Commission198114-37) The remaining 16 stories are part of the spire, which is capped by an observatory on the 102nd floor; the spire does not contain any intermediate levels and is used mostly for mechanical purposes.[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWillisFriedman199814-34) Atop the 102nd story is the 203 ft (61.9 m) pinnacle, much of which is covered by broadcast antennas, and surmounted with a [lightning rod](/wiki/Lightning_rod "Lightning rod").[[35]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJackson2010413–414-38)

fanoutqa_034536.x:
Pete Conrad :: Death :: chunk_0008
Conrad died on July 8, 1999, from internal injuries sustained in a motorcycle accident. While traveling with his wife and friends from his [Huntington Beach](/wiki/Huntington_Beach,_California "Huntington Beach, California") home to [Monterey, California](/wiki/Monterey,_California "Monterey, California"), his motorcycle crashed on a turn. Conrad later died in a hospital in [Ojai](/wiki/Ojai,_California "Ojai, California").[[30]](#cite_note-30) He was wearing a helmet at the time and was operating within the speed limit.[[3]](#cite_note-NYT-3) He was buried with full honours at [Arlington National Cemetery](/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery"),[[31]](#cite_note-31) with many Apollo-era astronauts in attendance and a performance of "[Amazing Grace](/wiki/Amazing_Grace "Amazing Grace")" by music legend [Willie Nelson](/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson").[[32]](#cite_note-32)

The [Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center](/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in [Houston, Texas](/wiki/Houston,_Texas "Houston, Texas"), has a grove of trees that have been planted to honor the memory of the astronauts who have died. After Conrad's death, [NASA](/wiki/NASA "NASA") planted a tree in his honor. During the dedication ceremony, his [Apollo 12](/wiki/Apollo_12 "Apollo 12") crewmate [Alan Bean](/wiki/Alan_Bean "Alan Bean") used his speech to lighten the sombre occasion by injecting a little levity, pretending to "channel" Conrad's instructions from the hereafter. Bean said Conrad wanted NASA to light his tree every Christmas season with coloured lights instead of the white used for everyone else, in keeping with his motto "when you can't be good, be colourful". NASA has honoured this request, and every Christmas since then, all of the trees in the grove have been lit with white lights—except Conrad's tree, which has been lit with red lights.[[2]](#cite_note-rocketman-2): xiii[[33]](#cite_note-33)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/%22Cristiano_Ronaldo%22_%285098214382%29.jpg/250px-%22Cristiano_Ronaldo%22_%285098214382%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:%22Cristiano_Ronaldo%22_(5098214382).jpg)

At his peak, Ronaldo was known for his exceptional speed, explosive shooting, flair and athleticism.[[253]](#cite_note-257)

A versatile [attacker](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)"), Ronaldo is capable of playing on either wing as well as through the centre of the pitch,[[254]](#cite_note-258) and, while ostensibly right-footed, is very strong with both feet.[[255]](#cite_note-259) Tactically, Ronaldo has undergone several evolutions throughout his career. While at Sporting and during his first season at Manchester United, he was typically deployed as a traditional [winger](/wiki/Midfielder#Winger "Midfielder") on the right side of midfield, where he regularly looked to deliver [crosses](/wiki/Cross_(football) "Cross (football)") into the penalty area. In this position, he was able to use his pace and acceleration, agility and technical skills to take on opponents in one-on-one situations. Ronaldo became noted for his [dribbling](/wiki/Dribbling#Association_football "Dribbling") and flair, often displaying an array of [tricks](/wiki/Association_football_tactics_and_skills "Association football tactics and skills") and [feints](/wiki/Dummy_(football) "Dummy (football)"),[[256]](#cite_note-Bolt-260)[[257]](#cite_note-261) such as the [step overs](/wiki/Step_over "Step over") and so-called 'chops' that became his trademark;[[258]](#cite_note-Grantland-262) he has also been known to use the [flip-flap](/wiki/Flip_flap_(association_football) "Flip flap (association football)").[[259]](#cite_note-263)

His strength and jumping ability, combined with his elevation, heading accuracy and height of 1.87 m (6 ft 1+1⁄2 in), give him an edge in winning aerial duels. These attributes allow him to function as a target-man and make him an aerial goal threat in the penalty area; consequently, many of his goals have been headers.[[260]](#cite_note-Molinaro-264)[

Spanish is the primary language in 20 countries worldwide. As of 2025, it is estimated that about 519 million people speak Spanish as a [native language](/wiki/First_language "First language"), making it the second [most spoken language by number of native speakers](/wiki/List_of_languages_by_number_of_native_speakers "List of languages by number of native speakers").[[29]](#cite_note-29) An additional 117 million speak Spanish as a second or [foreign language](/wiki/Spanish_as_a_foreign_language "Spanish as a foreign language"), making it the fourth [most spoken language in the world overall](/wiki/List_of_languages_by_total_number_of_speakers "List of languages by total number of speakers") after English, Mandarin Chinese, and Hindi with a total number of 636 million speakers.[[30]](#cite_note-30) Spanish is also the third [most used language on the Internet](/wiki/Languages_used_on_the_Internet "Languages used on the Internet"), after English and Chinese.[[31]](#cite_note-31)

fanoutqa_036072.t: Philadelphia Flyers :: History :: Broad Street Bullies (1971–1981) :: 1973–74 Stanley Cup champions :: chunk_0006

Philadelphia Flyers :: History :: Broad Street Bullies (1971–1981) :: 1973–74 Stanley Cup champions :: chunk_0006
Goaltender Bernie Parent returned to the franchise in the off-season, and the Flyers proved that the expansion teams could challenge the Original Six in [1973–74](/wiki/1973%E2%80%9374_NHL_season "1973–74 NHL season"). The Bullies continued their rough-and-tumble ways, led by Dave Schultz's 348 penalty minutes, and reached the top of the [West Division](/wiki/West_Division_(NHL) "West Division (NHL)") with a record of 50–16–12. The return of Parent proved to be of great benefit, as he established himself as one of if not the best goaltender in the league after winning 47 games, a record which stood for 33 years.[[27]](#cite_note-WhatAboutBob-29) Since the Flyers, along with Chicago, allowed the fewest goals in the league, Parent also shared the [Vezina Trophy](/wiki/Vezina_Trophy "Vezina Trophy") with Chicago's [Tony Esposito](/wiki/Tony_Esposito "Tony Esposito").

Come playoff time, the Flyers swept the Atlanta Flames in four games in the first round. In the semifinals, the Flyers faced the [New York Rangers](/wiki/New_York_Rangers "New York Rangers"). The series, which saw the home team win every game, went seven games. Fortunately for the Flyers, they had [home-ice advantage](/wiki/Home_advantage "Home advantage") as they advanced to the [Stanley Cup Final](/wiki/1974_Stanley_Cup_Final "1974 Stanley Cup Final") by winning game seven and in the process made history by becoming the first expansion team to win a playoff series over an Original Six team.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Bob_Clarke_2012.jpg/250px-Bob_Clarke_2012.jpg)](/wiki/File:Bob_Clarke_2012.jpg)

[Bobby Clarke](/wiki/Bobby_Clarke "Bobby Clarke") played for the Flyers from 1969 to 1984.

Their opponent, [Bobby Orr](/wiki/Bobby_Orr "Bobby Orr") and the Boston Bruins, took game one in Boston, but Bobby Clarke scored an overtime goal in game two to even the series. Education in the United Kingdom is a [devolved](/wiki/Devolution "Devolution") matter, with each country having a separate education system. About 38 per cent of the United Kingdom population has a university or [college degree](/wiki/College_degree "College degree"), the highest percentage in Europe and one of the highest in the world.[[407]](#cite_note-428) The UK is home to [many universities](/wiki/List_of_universities_in_the_United_Kingdom "List of universities in the United Kingdom"), including the [University of Oxford](/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") and [University of Cambridge](/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge"), which often achieve first place on global rankings.[[408]](#cite_note-429)[[409]](#cite_note-430)

University education has varied [tuition fees](/wiki/Student_loans_and_grants_in_the_United_Kingdom "Student loans and grants in the United Kingdom") in different regions of the UK. England and Wales have a fixed maximum annual fee for all UK citizens, contingent on attaining a certain level of income. Only those who reach a certain salary threshold pay this fee through [general taxation](/wiki/Taxation_in_the_United_Kingdom "Taxation in the United Kingdom").[[410]](#cite_note-431) Northern Ireland and Scotland have a reduced maximum fee or no fee for citizens where it is their home region. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/JTU_Students_and_Teachers_moved_to_Xi%27an_in_1956.jpg/250px-JTU_Students_and_Teachers_moved_to_Xi%27an_in_1956.jpg)](/wiki/File:JTU_Students_and_Teachers_moved_to_Xi%27an_in_1956.jpg)

The first students and teachers started to move to Xi'an in 1956

The national strategy adopted in 1956 dictated that the majority of Jiao Tong University would be moved to Xi'an, Shaanxi ([Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 交通大学西迁). During the movement, the national strategy was changed and there were questions on necessity of the move. Since the majority of the facilities, staffs, faculties and students had already arrived in [Xi'an](/wiki/Xi%27an "Xi'an") and the campus had started operated, the university decided to operate two campuses, one in [Xi'an](/wiki/Xi%27an "Xi'an") and another in [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"). However, the operation with two campuses were difficult and moving the [Xi'an](/wiki/Xi%27an "Xi'an") campus back to [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") was impossible. Thus, from July 31, 1959, with the approval from [State Council of the People's Republic of China](/wiki/State_Council_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "State Council of the People's Republic of China"), two campuses became independent. The Xi'an campus changed its name to Xi'an Jiaotong University and the Shanghai campus changed its name to [Shanghai Jiao Tong University](/wiki/Shanghai_Jiao_Tong_University "Shanghai Jiao Tong University"). Xi'an Jiaotong University was immediately listed as a [National Key University](/wiki/National_Key_Universities "National Key Universities"). Later, it became one of a handful of universities built according to the "Seventh Five-Year Plan" and "Eighth Five-Year Plan." In 2000, the State Council approved a merger of Xi'an Medical University and the Shaanxi Institute of Finance and Economics into Xi'an Jiaotong University.

Xi'an Jiaotong University has been part of all major government efforts to establish world-class universities in China, including [Project 211](/wiki/Project_211 "Project 211"), [Project 985]

fanoutqa_025064.t: OPEC :: History and impact :: 2021: Saudi-Emirati dispute :: chunk_0018
fanoutqa_025064.x:
OPEC :: History and impact :: 2021: Saudi-Emirati dispute :: chunk_0018
In July 2021, OPEC+ member United Arab Emirates rejected a Saudi proposed eight-month extension to oil output curbs which was in place due to [COVID-19](/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and lower oil consumption.[[154]](#cite_note-154)[[155]](#cite_note-155) The previous year, OPEC+ cut the equivalent of about 10% of demand at the time. The UAE asked for the maximum amount of oil the group would recognize the country of producing to be raised to 3.8 million barrels a day compared to its previous 3.2 million barrels. A compromise deal allowed UAE to increase its maximum oil output to 3.65 million barrels a day.[[156]](#cite_note-156)

Under the terms of the agreement, Russia would increase its production from 11 million barrels to 11.5 million by May 2022 as well. All members would increase output by 400,000 barrels per day each month starting in August to gradually offset the previous cuts made due to the COVID pandemic.[[157]](#cite_note-157)

This compromise, achieved where Saudi Arabia met the United Arab Emirates halfway, underscored OPEC+ unity. UAE Energy Minister [Suhail Al-Mazrouei](/wiki/Suhail_Al_Mazroui "Suhail Al Mazroui") thanked Saudi Arabia and Russia for facilitating dialogue leading to an agreement. He stated, "The UAE is committed to this group and will always work with it." On the Saudi side, Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman emphasized consensus building and stated that the agreement strengthens OPEC+'s ties and ensures its continuity.[[158]](#cite_note-158)
